title: OpenWiz vs OpenHands
description: Compare OpenWiz’s GitHub-based factory with OpenHands Agent Canvas and SDK on licensing, runtimes, tracking, review and pricing.
answer: OpenWiz is an open source agent factory that coordinates coding agents around specs and tickets in GitHub. OpenHands offers Agent Canvas for running coding agents in conversations and a Software Agent SDK for building agents into your own tools.

sections.heading: At a glance
sections.body:
| | OpenWiz | OpenHands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open source and licence | Open source under Apache-2.0. [OpenWiz README](https://github.com/openwizdev/OpenWiz/blob/09ad084f81023de18f2cd3b9f1967d9abb7f5c89/README.md). | Agent Canvas is open source under MIT. The pricing page lists separate Teams and Enterprise plans. [OpenHands pricing](https://www.openhands.dev/pricing), checked 2026-11-28. |
| Where agents run | On your computer or VPS, in a boat.dev sandbox, or in a CloudRoom thread. [OpenWiz 0.1.0 changelog](https://github.com/openwizdev/OpenWiz/blob/09ad084f81023de18f2cd3b9f1967d9abb7f5c89/CHANGELOG.md#010--2026-11-21). | Agent Canvas can use a local backend, Docker, a VM or an OpenHands Cloud sandbox. [Agent Canvas overview](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/agent-canvas/overview), checked 2026-11-28. |
| Which agents | The local driver runs Claude Code or Codex using your existing sign-in. [OpenWiz 0.1.0 changelog](https://github.com/openwizdev/OpenWiz/blob/09ad084f81023de18f2cd3b9f1967d9abb7f5c89/CHANGELOG.md#010--2026-11-21). | OpenHands runs agents built with its Software Agent SDK. Agent Canvas can also connect Claude Code or Codex via the Agent Client Protocol. [OpenHands introduction](https://docs.openhands.dev/overview/introduction), checked 2026-11-28. |
| How work is tracked | GitHub issues hold specs, tickets and agent status. Pull requests and reviews stay on GitHub. [How OpenWiz works](https://github.com/openwizdev/OpenWiz/blob/09ad084f81023de18f2cd3b9f1967d9abb7f5c89/docs/how-openwiz-works.md). | Agent Canvas tracks each session as a conversation with message history, tool calls and file changes. It can also start work from GitHub Issues, Jira or Linear. [Agent Canvas conversations](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/agent-canvas/conversations), checked 2026-11-28. [Issue to Pull Request Automation](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/agent-canvas/prebuilt/issue-to-pr), checked 2026-11-28. |
| Review | In 0.1.0 the CloudRoom fleet routes green pull requests to a separate reviewer when available. With local or boat.dev builders, you review pull requests yourself. [How OpenWiz works](https://github.com/openwizdev/OpenWiz/blob/09ad084f81023de18f2cd3b9f1967d9abb7f5c89/docs/how-openwiz-works.md). | Agent Canvas offers a prebuilt automation that watches GitHub pull requests and has an OpenHands agent review them. [GitHub PR Review Assistant](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/agent-canvas/prebuilt/github-pr-review), checked 2026-11-28. |
| Price | The software is free. You pay your own model and host charges. [OpenWiz README](https://github.com/openwizdev/OpenWiz/blob/09ad084f81023de18f2cd3b9f1967d9abb7f5c89/README.md). | The open source edition is free to self-host and uses your own model key. OpenHands Cloud is free with conversation limits. Self-hosted Teams starts at $500/month and Enterprise pricing is custom. [OpenHands pricing](https://www.openhands.dev/pricing), checked 2026-11-28. [OpenHands Cloud overview](https://docs.openhands.dev/overview/introduction), checked 2026-11-28. |

sections.heading: Where OpenHands fits better
sections.body: Choose OpenHands if you want a workspace that keeps each agent session’s messages and file changes together, or a Python SDK for embedding coding agents in your own software. [Agent Canvas conversations](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/agent-canvas/conversations), checked 2026-11-28. [Software Agent SDK overview](https://docs.openhands.dev/overview/introduction), checked 2026-11-28.

sections.heading: Where OpenWiz fits better
sections.body: Choose OpenWiz when you want to organize a fleet around an approved spec and its tickets, with decisions, agent status, pull requests and reviews recorded in GitHub. [How OpenWiz works](https://github.com/openwizdev/OpenWiz/blob/09ad084f81023de18f2cd3b9f1967d9abb7f5c89/docs/how-openwiz-works.md).

faq.question: Can both tools use Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. OpenWiz’s local driver runs the Claude Code or Codex you already sign in to. Agent Canvas connects them through the Agent Client Protocol.

faq.question: Can I try OpenHands without installing Agent Canvas?
faq.answer: Yes. OpenHands Cloud provides a hosted version of Agent Canvas with limits on how many conversations you can run.

sources.supports: OpenWiz is an open source agent factory under Apache-2.0. The software is free, and users cover their own model and host charges.
GitHub records specs, tickets, pull requests and reviews. In OpenWiz 0.1.0 the CloudRoom fleet can route pull requests to separate reviewers. Local and boat.dev pull requests are reviewed by hand.
OpenWiz 0.1.0 offers builders on your computer or VPS, on boat.dev, or in CloudRoom. The local driver uses Claude Code or Codex with your own sign-in.

OpenHands provides Agent Canvas for agent conversations and a Python SDK for building or embedding agents. Canvas connects Claude Code and Codex through ACP. OpenHands Cloud is free with conversation limits.
OpenHands lists MIT licensing for its free self-hosted edition, a bring-your-own model key, and prices for Teams and Enterprise.
Agent Canvas can run agents through a local backend, Docker, a VM or OpenHands Cloud.
An Agent Canvas conversation records its own message history, tool calls and file changes.
The GitHub PR Review Assistant lets Agent Canvas monitor pull requests and ask an OpenHands agent to review them.
OpenHands can start agent work from ready issues in GitHub Issues, Jira or Linear.

better_fit: Choose OpenHands if you want a workspace that keeps each agent session’s messages and file changes together, or a Python SDK for embedding coding agents in your own software.
